name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap query engine)
description: A query language over the entire OpenStreetMap database: every cafe in a bounding box, every trail with a given surface tag, every building within 500 m of a school. This is the closest thing there is to a free global spatial database you can ask arbitrary questions of.

access.size_hint: a city-sized amenity query is a few hundred KB; a country-sized one can be gigabytes and will be refused
access.rate_limit: slot-based, not request-based: GET /api/status tells you your rate limit, slots available and current load
access.etiquette: always put [timeout:25] in the query and bound it by bbox or area; unbounded queries are what get instances overloaded

probes.description: Your slot allocation and the server's load
A deliberately tiny query - large ones 504 under load
probes.note: The public instance answers 504 whenever it is busy, which is often. A failure here is usually load, not breakage - check the status probe beside it.

recipes.title: Every cafe in a bounding box
recipes.code:
curl -s -G https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter \
  --data-urlencode 'data=[out:json][timeout:25];node(39.02,-77.09,39.04,-77.06)[amenity=cafe];out body;' \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(e['tags'].get('name'), e['lat'], e['lon']) for e in json.load(sys.stdin)['elements']]"

gotchas.trap: HTTP 504 from the public instance usually means the server was busy, not that your query was wrong. The same query often succeeds a minute later or with a smaller bbox.
gotchas.fix: Check /api/status first, keep [timeout:25] in the query, and back off rather than retrying immediately.

gotchas.trap: Query results are nodes, ways and relations, not features. A building is a way whose geometry is a list of node ids.
gotchas.fix: Ask for 'out geom;' or 'out center;' unless you want to resolve node references yourself.
